What it is
- “Pre-Bond Planning Update” presentation to the Troy Board of Education, September 7, 2021.

Process components
- Survey Data Collection (May-July 2021): gathered beliefs on the current state from the Board, Cabinet, instructional leadership, teachers, and students.
- Facilities Assessment (May-September 2021): assessment of all district facilities (floors, doors, windows, HVAC, roofs, etc.), conducted by Barton Malow.
- Guiding Principles (July-August 2021): broad vision statements built from those used in the Early Childhood Center design (flexible learning spaces, natural light, eco-friendly, universal design, career exploration).
- Welcome Back Admin Kickoff (August 2021): keynote by Dr. Tony Wagner on modern learning, the future of work, and High Tech High.
- Program Assessment (August-September 2021): how buildings support programming, conducted by the TMP architectural team with building principals.

Facilities Review Committee
- Application opened September 1, closes September 15; 60 applications as of 9/7/21.

Up next
- October 5 update to the Board with summary presentations: Facilities Assessment (Barton Malow) and Program Assessment (TMP).
https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.verbose:
This “Pre-Bond Planning Update” presentation was delivered to the Troy Board of Education on September 7, 2021, describing the comprehensive process underway to inform a potential future bond proposal.

Survey Data Collection (May-July 2021): The district gathered beliefs on the current state and insight from end users to begin identifying “look-fors” for the program assessment and to share feedback with building administrators. Participants included the Board of Education, Cabinet, instructional leadership, teachers, and students, capturing student and teacher perspectives.

Facilities Assessment (May-September 2021): An assessment of all district facilities focused on “bricks and mortar” — floors, doors, windows, HVAC, roofs, and more — was conducted by Barton Malow, with a presentation to the Board being prepared for October 5.

Guiding Principles (July-August 2021): Broad vision statements were developed to guide “look-fors” during the program assessment, built from vision statements used in the design of the Early Childhood Center. They call for spaces that encourage curiosity, movement, and exploration; convenient, direct, safe, and welcoming access for students and parents; schools organized into smaller learning communities supporting belonging, collaboration, inclusion, and equity; flexible, adaptable, and stimulating learning spaces; abundant natural light in all instructional spaces; “eco-friendly” design allowing interaction with the natural environment; professional space for teacher teaming and collaboration; accessibility for all through universal design; spaces for career exploration and community partnerships; and flexible furnishings to transform classrooms into “flexible learning studios” for hands-on, project-based learning.

Welcome Back Admin Kickoff (August 2021): Featured a keynote by Dr. Tony Wagner on modern learning, the future of work, and High Tech High.

Program Assessment (August-September 2021): An assessment of how buildings function to support school programming, conducted by the TMP architectural team in collaboration with building principals and admin teams, driven by the Guiding Principles concepts of flexible, inclusive, collaborative, and accessible. A presentation to the Board was being prepared for October 5.

Facilities Review Committee Application (September 2021): The application opened September 1 and closes September 15; as of September 7, 2021, 60 applications had been received.

Up Next: An October 5 update to the Board of Education, featuring summary presentations of the Facilities Assessment (Barton Malow) and the Program Assessment (TMP).

https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.paragraph: A presentation of Project 2026 Blueprint, Troy School District's World Class for All strategic plan, shared with the Board of Education on September 21, 2021. Built on the mission Ensuring learning for all and the OneTroy community, the plan is organized around four color-coded pillars: Early Childhood to Career (Green), Equity and Well-Being (Red), Deep Learning (Blue), and Building Capacity (Gold), each with objectives and measurable key results tied to the core values of Collaboration, Deep Learning, and Focus.
https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.page:
What it is
- Slide deck introducing Project 2026 Blueprint, the Troy School District World Class for All strategic plan, presented to the Board on September 21, 2021.
- Frames a mission/vision refresh and an accountability plan structured as Objectives and Key Results (OKRs).

Mission and values
- Mission: Ensuring learning for all, centering the OneTroy community.
- Core values: Collaboration, Deep Learning, Focus.

Four pillars
- Green - Early Childhood to Career: invest in early childhood education, advocate for universal preschool for three- and four-year-olds, and expand college and career pathways and CTE. Key results include applying for 16-32 additional GSRP slots in 2021-22, opening 2-3 new PreK classrooms (40-60 students), legislator meetings on free preschool, and developing a Portrait of a Graduate framework and survey.
- Red - Equity and Well-Being: safely reopen schools, support the whole child with wraparound services, and hire more counselors, social workers, and school psychologists; assess facilities upgrades.
- Blue - Deep Learning: build systems that deepen learning and student voice, improve technology access and training, monitor instructional data at least 3 times per year, and expand job-embedded coaching.
- Gold - Building Capacity: strengthen educator pipelines (including underrepresented educators), provide job-embedded professional learning, and implement a 90-minute Delayed Start model for staff collaboration.

Purpose
- Communicate the refreshed strategic direction and measurable goals for students, staff, and the community.
https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.verbose:
A slide presentation introducing Project 2026 Blueprint, the Troy School District World Class for All strategic plan, shared with the Board of Education at the September 21, 2021 Regular Meeting. The deck frames a mission and vision refresh, key themes and next steps, and an accountability plan built on Objectives and Key Results.

The stated District mission is Ensuring learning for all, centering the OneTroy community, and the World Class for All pillars are aligned to core values of Collaboration, Deep Learning, and Focus. Four color-coded pillars organize the plan, each presented with an overview, objectives, and key results.

Green Pillar - Early Childhood to Career: objectives include continuing to invest in high-quality early childhood education, advocating for universal preschool for all three- and four-year-olds and access for all, and expanding college and career pathways for middle and high school students through high-quality career and technical education, expanded computer science access, connections for underrepresented students to in-demand high-growth careers, and partnerships with higher education and employers offering work-based learning, credentials, and college credit. Key results include applying for 16-32 additional GSRP (Great Start Readiness Program) slots from the State of Michigan in 2021-22, opening an additional 2-3 PreK classrooms (40-60 students) in 2021-22, scheduling two meetings or site visits with local legislators regarding free preschool for all, having building leaders participate in Career Readiness meetings twice during the year, researching a Portrait of a Graduate framework, and developing a Portrait of a Graduate survey by the close of 2021-22.

Red Pillar - Equity and Well-Being: overview items include safely reopening schools and supporting students disproportionately impacted by the pandemic; funding investments to support the whole child, including community schools that provide wraparound services such as afterschool programs and hiring more counselors, social workers, and school psychologists; and assessing the need and taking action for upgraded facilities. Key results emphasize increasing social work and counseling support in all buildings, reviewing and monitoring student data, emphasizing adult learning in the areas of well-being and equity, and creating a common understanding of a system of support at all levels.

Blue Pillar - Deep Learning: objectives include creating and sustaining systems of support that deepen learning and empower student voice, improving technology access for students and families with quality training, pursuing global best practices across content areas, and assessing and acting on facilities upgrades. Key results include monitoring instructional data at least three times per year, expanding job-embedded coaching, and leveraging technology for all students in all buildings.

Gold Pillar - Building Capacity of Students, Staff, and Families: objectives include improving educator preparation, strengthening pipelines for underrepresented educators, supporting current educators, continuing job-embedded professional learning for all staff, and providing professional learning for staff, community, and students to co-design impactful experiences for the OneTroy community. Key results include expanding hiring networks, expanding job-embedded coaching, and implementing a Delayed Start Model of 90 minutes to ensure collaboration through professional learning focused on advancing strategic-planning priorities. The extracted text ends mid-slide during the Gold Pillar key results.

https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.paragraph: A recognition item (2.D) from the September 21, 2021 regular meeting honoring Bemis and Troy Union Elementary Schools for receiving the 2021 National Schools of Character Award from Character.org. The two Troy schools were among just 47 nationwide to earn the distinction, recognized for using character development to positively affect academics, student behavior, and cultural climate under principals Jeremey Whan and Mike Cottone.
https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.page:
What it is
- Board recognition item (agenda item 2.D, dated 09.21.21) at the September 21, 2021 Regular Meeting.

The honor
- Bemis and Troy Union Elementary Schools received the 2021 National Schools of Character Award from Character.org, described as a national advocate and leader for character in education.
- The two schools were among only 47 schools across the country to receive the distinction.
- They were recognized for demonstrating use of character development to drive a positive impact on academics, student behavior, and cultural climate - promoting good character, culture, and ethics; fostering student self-motivation; giving students the opportunity for moral action; and engaging families and community members as partners.

Who
- Principals Jeremey Whan (Bemis) and Mike Cottone (Troy Union).

Action
- Recommended action: the Board recognizes Jeremey Whan and Mike Cottone and any staff members in attendance, presenting a certificate from the Board of Education.

A recognition item (agenda item 2.D, dated 09.21.21) from the Troy School District Board of Education's September 21, 2021 Regular Meeting, honoring Bemis and Troy Union Elementary Schools for receiving the 2021 National Schools of Character Award.

The item explains that Bemis and Troy Union are two of 47 schools across the country to receive this important distinction from Character.org, described as a national advocate and leader for character in education. The program recognized the two schools as having demonstrated their use of character development to drive a positive impact on academics, student behavior, and cultural climate. Under the leadership of Principals Jeremey Whan and Mike Cottone, the committee praised Bemis and Troy Union for promoting good character, culture, and ethics; fostering student self-motivation; giving students the opportunity for moral action; and engaging families and community members as partners in character-building efforts.

The Board invited Mr. Whan and Mr. Cottone up to receive a certificate from the Board of Education. The recommended action is that the Board recognizes Jeremey Whan and Mike Cottone and any staff members in attendance with them.

A recognition item (agenda item 2.E, dated 09.21.21) from the Troy School District Board of Education's September 21, 2021 Regular Meeting, presenting several Michigan Association of School Boards (MASB) awards received during the prior year as a result of the Board's commitment to excellence in governance.

The individual honors are: Trustee Vital Anne, who achieved the Award of Merit, which requires the completion of all Level 1 courses and 45 education credits; Trustee Elizabeth Hammond, who received the Advocacy Skills Specialty Award; and Trustee Dr. Nancy Philippart, who received the Data Skill Specialty Award (also referred to as the Data Specialty Award). In addition, the entire Board earned the Honor Board Award and the Standard of Excellence Award.

The item states that all of these honors place the Troy Board of Education among a handful of other Michigan school district governing bodies that have demonstrated a true commitment to student achievement and exemplary leadership, and notes that the Troy community is fortunate to have seven Board members who are committed to the concept of life-long learning and positive policy making. The recommended action is to present the awards.
